observations.explanation: The paper describes high-level natural-language tasks and functional-correctness checks that assess outcomes rather than matching action sequences, allowing alternative valid paths (PDF p. 2).

The environment supports observations as HTML, screenshots, or accessibility trees, includes multi-tab browsing and interactive actions, and is presented as a platform for agent development (PDF pp. 2, 4–5).

The authors report low success rates and analyze distinct failure patterns, including erroneous infeasibility judgments and observation-interpretation failures, giving the results diagnostic value (PDF pp. 9–11).
The results compare direct and reasoning prompt styles; the direct agent is reported with GPT-3.5, while the reasoning agent is reported with GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 (PDF p. 9).
